name: Question 15
problem:
The velocity $v$ at time $t$ of a particle $P$ moving in the $xy$-plane is given by

$$
v(t)=⟨4t,3{t}^{2}-1⟩\,,\,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).
$$

Given that the particle is at the position  $r=⟨-2,0⟩$ when $t=0,$ calculate the times when the particle is at the origin.
worked_solution:
The particle is at the origin when its position is $r=⟨0,0⟩.$ So first, we need to compute the position function of the particle.

To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =\int v(t)\,\text{d}t \\  & =\int ⟨4t,3{t}^{2}-1⟩\,\text{d}t \\  & =⟨\int 4t\,\text{d}t,\,\int (3{t}^{2}-1)\text{d}t⟩ \\  & =⟨2{t}^{2}+{C}_{1},\,{t}^{3}-t+{C}_{2}⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that $r(0)=⟨-2,0⟩.$ Substituting $t=0,$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r(0) & =⟨2(0)^{2}+{C}_{1},\,{0}^{3}-0+{C}_{2}⟩ \\ ⟨-2,0⟩ & =⟨{C}_{1},\,{C}_{2}⟩,\end{aligned}
$$

so we must have ${C}_{1}=-2$ and ${C}_{2}=0.$ Therefore, the position of $P$ at time $t$ is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨2{t}^{2}-2,\,{t}^{3}-t⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

To find the times at which the particle is at the origin, we solve the equation $r(t)=⟨0,0⟩.$

$$
\begin{aligned}r(t) & =⟨0,0⟩ \\ ⟨2{t}^{2}-2,\,{t}^{3}-t⟩ & =⟨0,0⟩.\end{aligned}
$$

So we need

$$
\begin{aligned}2{t}^{2}-2=2(t-1)(t+1) & =0\,⇒\,t=\pm 1, \\ {t}^{3}-t=t(t-1)(t+1) & =0\,⇒\,t=\pm 1,0.\end{aligned}
$$

The solutions that satisfy both equations are $t=\pm 1.$ Therefore, we conclude that the particle is at the origin  when $t=\pm 1.$

Question 15
?

The velocity v at time t of a particle P moving in the xy-plane is given by v(t)=⟨4t,3t2−1⟩,t∈(−∞,∞). Given that the particle is at the position r=⟨−2,0⟩ when t=0, calculate the times when the particle is at the origin.

a
t=±1
b
The particle is never at the origin
c
t=−1,0
d
t=±1,0
e
t=0,1
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

The particle is at the origin when its position is r=⟨0,0⟩. So first, we need to compute the position function of the particle.

To compute the position vector, we need to integrate the velocity vector:

r(t)=∫v(t)dt=∫⟨4t,3t2−1⟩dt=⟨∫4tdt,∫(3t2−1)dt⟩=⟨2t2+C1,t3−t+C2⟩

Now, we can solve for the constants of integration using the fact that r(0)=⟨−2,0⟩. Substituting t=0, we get

r(0)=⟨2(0)2+C1,03−0+C2⟩⟨−2,0⟩=⟨C1,C2⟩,

so we must have C1=−2 and C2=0. Therefore, the position of P at time t is given by

r(t)=⟨2t2−2,t3−t⟩.

To find the times at which the particle is at the origin, we solve the equation r(t)=⟨0,0⟩.

r(t)=⟨0,0⟩⟨2t2−2,t3−t⟩=⟨0,0⟩.

So we need 2t2−2=2(t−1)(t+1)=0⇒t=±1,t3−t=t(t−1)(t+1)=0⇒t=±1,0.

The solutions that satisfy both equations are t=±1. Therefore, we conclude that the particle is at the origin when t=±1.
